sentences.text: Orodromeus is a small, herbivorous dinosaur belonging to the family Thescelosauridae that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous.
The genus name Orodromeus means "Mountain Runner" and refers to the animal's cursorial (running) habits and the Egg Mountain discovery site.
Horner and Weishampel estimated the length of Orodromeus to be 2.5 meters.
Orodromeus apparently possessed a strong jugal bone similar to that of Zephyrosaurus.
Ten nests of Orodromeus have been found, containing eggs arranged in a spiral pattern.
CT scans of unhatched Orodromeus eggs showed well-developed embryos, unlike those of Maiasaura which hatched helpless.
The unhatched eggshells were not trampled, indicating that the young abandoned the nest immediately upon hatching.
Fossils of Orodromeus were discovered by Robert Makela in Teton County, Montana, while excavating a nesting colony of Maiasaura.
The species Orodromeus makelai was named and described by Jack Horner and David B. Weishampel in 1988.
The holotype specimen was found in the Campanian stage of the Two Medicine Formation, approximately 75 million years ago.
The specific name makelai honors Robert Makela, who died in a car accident shortly after discovering the fossils.
Jack Horner concluded that Orodromeus young were precocial based on the advanced development of their bones and teeth.
Orodromeus nested in large colonies where individual nests were excavated and covered to better control temperature.
It appears that Orodromeus parents cared for their nests by driving away small predators.
Researchers speculate that Orodromeus may have burrowed, similar to its relative Oryctodromeus, based on the unusual packing of its fossil bones.
Modern classification views Orodromeus as a basal member of the Euornithopoda, as the group Hypsilophodontidae is considered unnatural and paraphyletic.
Brown et al. (2013) classified Orodromeus in the family Thescelosauridae and named the subfamily Orodrominae after it.
Orodromeus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
This small herbivore likely coexisted with dinosaurs such as Daspletosaurus and Einiosaurus.
Several Orodromeus nests were found alongside those of Maiasaura.
